correctness.rationale: For a zero-mass signed measure, midpoint centering gives exact sup norm osc/2; the full BL dual is the supremum over a truncated-metric one-Lipschitz problem divided by 1+r/2. Constructing the hierarchical tree with edge lengths (min(parent,r)-min(child,r))/2 makes the leaf distance exactly min(d,r). The cut-telescoping upper bound and explicit sign-of-subtree-mass potential attain F(r)=B(r)/2. Each B piece is affine, so B/(2+r) is monotone or constant between cluster heights; beyond the diameter it decreases. These steps prove the uniform theorem. Direct calculation gives the two-cluster switch at P=aS/(2+a). The standalone checker independently solved 180 general LPs, 90 two-cluster LPs, and 11 atomic-pair cases (281 passed). Numerical experiments are supplementary and do not establish the infinite family.

value.rationale: Finite ultrametrics are a standard nontrivial multiscale family for weak convergence metrics. The result turns the coupled bounded-Lipschitz optimization, previously approached via general norming sets or LP, into a direct O(n log n) tree sweep with explicit norming functions, exactly necessary cluster candidates, and a parameter-complete sharp two-scale phase boundary independent of between-cluster separation. This is a substantive structural classification with clear practical computation and interpretability, not a renamed classical W1 identity.
